'''Lucien Szpiro''' (23 December 1941&nbsp;– 18 April 2020) was a French mathematician known for his work in [[number theory]], [[arithmetic geometry]], and [[commutative algebra]]. He formulated [[Szpiro's conjecture]] and was a distinguished professor at the [[CUNY Graduate Center]] and an emeritus {{ill|Director of Research|fr|Directeur de recherche au CNRS}} at the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research]].

==Early life and education==
Lucien Szpiro was born on 23 December 1941 in Paris, France.<ref name=CV>{{cite web |url=https://www.gc.cuny.edu/CUNY_GC/media/CUNY-Graduate-Center/PDF/Programs/Math/CVFall2010.pdf |title=Curriculum Vitae |date=2010 |access-date=19 April 2020 |archive-date=6 December 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211206083326/https://www.gc.cuny.edu/CUNY_GC/media/CUNY-Graduate-Center/PDF/Programs/Math/CVFall2010.pdf |url-status=dead}}</ref> Szpiro attended [[Paris-Sud University]] where he earned his [[Doctor of Philosophy]] under [[Pierre Samuel]].<ref name=CV/><ref name=mgp>{{MathGenealogy|id=37670|title=Lucien Szpiro}}</ref> His doctoral work was heavily influenced by the seminars of [[Maurice Auslander]], [[Claude Chevalley]], and [[Alexander Grothendieck]].<ref name=CV/> He earned his [[Habilitation#France|Doctorat d'État]] (DrE) in 1971.<ref name=CV/>

==Career==
From 1963 to 1965, Szpiro worked as an assistant high school teacher in Paris.<ref name=CV/><ref name=ae/> From 1965 to 1969, he was an assistant professor (''maître assistant'') at the [[University of Paris]].<ref name=CV/><ref name=ae/> From 1969 to 1999, Szpiro worked at the CNRS, initially as an [[Academic ranks in France#Temporary positions|attaché]] at [[Paris Diderot University]] before rising to the rank of a distinguished professor (''Directeur de Recherche de Classe Exceptionnelle'') at [[Paris-Sud University]].<ref name=ae/> In 1999, he became an emeritus professor (''Directeur de Recherche émérite'') at the CNRS and moved to the CUNY Graduate Center as a distinguished professor.<ref name=CV/><ref name=ae/><ref name=GS>{{cite web |url=https://www.gc.cuny.edu/Faculty/Core-Bios/Lucien-Szpiro |website=[[Graduate Center, CUNY]] |title=Lucien Szpiro |access-date=18 April 2020}}</ref> He also held visiting positions at several institutions including [[Columbia University]] and the [[Institute for Advanced Study]].<ref name=ae/><ref name="IAS">{{cite web |url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/lucien-szpiro |title=Lucien Szpiro |website=[[Institute for Advanced Study]] |date=9 December 2019 |access-date=19 April 2020}}</ref>

Szpiro was the editor-in-chief of ''[[Astérisque]]'' from 1991 to 1993 and an editor of the ''[[Bulletin de la Société Mathématique de France]]'' from 1984 to 1990.<ref name=CV/> He was also head of the commission that oversaw the [[Société mathématique de France]] libraries.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.enssib.fr/bibliotheque-numerique/documents/62615-reseau-de-bibliotheques-specialisees-le-reseau-des-bibliotheques-de-mathematiquesmemoire-d-etude-un.pdf?telecharger=1 |title=Un réseau de biblithèques spécialisées: le réseau des bibliothèques de mathematiques |website=[[École Nationale Supérieure des Sciences de l'Information et des Bibliothèques]] |date=1992 |access-date=19 April 2020 |language=fr |quote=Lucien Szpiro, responsable de la commission des bibliothèques de la SMF, estime que le cout de l'operation serait de 100 000 francs par an pour un reseau ne contenant que des listes de livres et de preprints.}}</ref>

Szpiro advised 17 doctoral students, including [[Ahmed Abbes]], [[Emmanuel Ullmo]], and [[Shou-Wu Zhang]].<ref name=CV/><ref name=mgp/>

==Research==
In the 1970s, Szpiro's research in commutative algebra led to his proof of the Auslander zero divisor conjecture.<ref name="IHES"/> Together with Christian Peskine, he developed the [[liaison theory]] of algebraic varieties.<ref name="IHES"/>

In the 1980s, Szpiro's research interests shifted to Diophantine geometry, first over [[algebraic function field|function fields]] and then over [[number field]]s.<ref name="IHES"/> The [[Institut des hautes études scientifiques]] described Szpiro as being "the first to realise the importance of a paper by Arakelov for questions of Diophantine geometry", which ultimately led to the development of [[Arakelov theory]] as a tool of modern [[Diophantine geometry]] exemplified by [[Gerd Faltings]]'s proof of the [[Faltings' theorem|Mordell conjecture]].<ref name=GS/><ref name="IHES"/> Szpiro also showed the link between the [[Ample line bundle|positivity]] of the [[dualising sheaf]] of a curve and the [[Bogomolov conjecture]].<ref name="IHES"/>

In 1981, Szpiro formulated a conjecture (now known as Szpiro's conjecture) relating the discriminant of an [[elliptic curve]] with its [[conductor of an elliptic curve|conductor]].<ref name="lang">{{cite book|first=Serge |last=Lang |author-link=Serge Lang |title=Survey of Diophantine geometry |publisher=[[Springer Science+Business Media|Springer-Verlag]] |location=Berlin |year=1997 |isbn=3-540-61223-8 | zbl=0869.11051 | page=51}}</ref> His conjecture inspired the [[abc conjecture|''abc'' conjecture]],<ref name="Fesenko">{{cite journal|title=Arithmetic deformation theory via arithmetic fundamental groups and nonarchimedean theta functions, notes on the work of Shinichi Mochizuki|journal=European Journal of Mathematics|first=Ivan|last=Fesenko|volume=1|issue=3|pages=405–440|year=2015|doi=10.1007/s40879-015-0066-0|s2cid=52085917|doi-access=free}}.</ref> which was later shown to be equivalent to a modified form of Szpiro's conjecture in 1988.<ref name="Oesterle-1988">{{cite journal| last=Oesterlé | first=Joseph | author-link=Joseph Oesterlé | title=Nouvelles approches du "théorème" de Fermat | url= http://www.numdam.org/item?id=SB_1987-1988__30__165_0 | series=Séminaire Bourbaki exp 694 |mr=992208 | year=1988 | journal=[[Astérisque]] | issn=0303-1179 | issue=161 | pages=165–186}}</ref> Szpiro's conjecture and its equivalent forms have been described as "the most important unsolved problem in [[Diophantine analysis]]" by [[Dorian Goldfeld]],<ref name="Goldfeld-1996">{{cite journal |last=Goldfeld |first=Dorian | author-link=Dorian M. Goldfeld |year=1996 |title=Beyond the last theorem |journal=[[Math Horizons]] |volume=4 |issue=September |pages=26–34 |jstor= 25678079 |doi=10.1080/10724117.1996.11974985}}</ref> in part to its large number of consequences in number theory including [[Roth's theorem]], the [[Faltings' theorem|Mordell conjecture]], the [[Fermat–Catalan conjecture]], and [[Brocard's problem]].<ref>{{cite journal | first1=Enrico | last1=Bombieri|author-link=Enrico Bombieri | title=Roth's theorem and the abc-conjecture | journal=Preprint | year=1994 | publisher=ETH Zürich}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Elkies |first=N. D. |author-link=Noam Elkies |title=ABC implies Mordell |journal= International Mathematics Research Notices|volume=1991 |year=1991 |pages=99–109 |doi=10.1155/S1073792891000144 |issue=7 |doi-access= <!-- not free--> }}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Pomerance |first=Carl |author-link=Carl Pomerance |chapter=Computational Number Theory |title=The Princeton Companion to Mathematics |publisher=[[Princeton University Press]] |year=2008 |pages=361–362}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |first=Andrzej |last=Dąbrowski |title=On the diophantine equation ''x''! + ''A'' = ''y''<sup>2</sup> | journal=Nieuw Archief voor Wiskunde, IV. |volume=14 |pages=321–324 |year=1996 | zbl=0876.11015}}</ref>

After moving to the CUNY Graduate Center in 1999, Szpiro began working on new research in [[arithmetic dynamics]].<ref name=GS/><ref name="IHES"/>

==Awards==
In 1987, Szpiro received the [[Prix Doistau–Blutel]] from the [[French Academy of Sciences]] "for his work in Commutative Algebra and Algebraic Geometry and for his contribution to G. Faltings’ proof of the [[Mordell conjecture]]."<ref name=GS/> In 2012 he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 5 August 2013.</ref> He was a [[Member of the Academia Europaea]].<ref name=ae>{{cite web |url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Szpiro_Lucien |website=[[Academia Europaea]] |title=Lucien Szpiro |access-date=18 April 2020}}</ref>

==Death==
Szpiro died on 18 April 2020 in Paris, France, from [[cardiac arrest]].<ref name=NEW>{{Cite web|url=https://www.math.columbia.edu/~woit/wordpress/?p=11717|title=Lucien Szpiro 1941–2020 &#124; Not Even Wrong|date=18 April 2020 }}</ref><ref name="IHES">{{cite web |url=https://www.ihes.fr/en/mathematician-lucien-szpiro-died-aged-78/ |title=Mathematician Lucien Szpiro passed away at the age of 78 |website=[[Institut des hautes études scientifiques]] |date=20 April 2020 |access-date=21 December 2020}}</ref>
